newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU to tell China not to threaten its members.
newsitem.headline: EU to tell China not to threaten its members.

text.p: Five European Union countries that broke ranks and failed to support a U.N. resolution critical of China are to tell Beijing not to retaliate against those in the bloc that supported the move.
Diplomats said that France, Germany, Spain, Italy and Greece pledged at an EU foreign ministers meeting on Tuesday to tell China that retaliation for support of the resolution was unacceptable.
The five countries backed off from supporting the EU's annual sponsorship of the resolution -- which condemns China for human-rights violations -- leaving the task of chief sponsor to Denmark.
Denmark and the Netherlands, the current EU president, say they are now coming under commercial pressure from China. Both appealed to fellow EU states for support.
China reacted furiously to Denmark's sponsorship of the annual resolution, which had U.S. support. Beijing blocked it on April 15.
Denmark decided to sponsor the resolution after France blocked agreement for the EU to support the resolution as a bloc. The other four abstained when the resolution came to a vote at the U.N.
Beijing responded initially by cancelling visits by Danish officials, but diplomats said other pressure is now being applied.
The EU ministers also authorised the Netherlands, as EU president, to inform Beijing that the five countries would be raising the issue at a high level.
